title: Wedding invitation wording — bilingual
context: Hungarian + English. Warm but not cheesy. Reflects the anti-performative values. 'Come celebrate with us' not 'request the honour of your presence'.

title: Handmade Paper Wedding Invitations
context: Letterpress on cotton paper — tactile, imperfect, beautiful. Each one slightly different. Deckled edges.

title: Outdoor ceremony with wildflower arch
context: No florist needed. Just gather wildflowers and build a simple arch. Impermanent, seasonal, real.

title: Second sourdough bake: much better rise! The ear is starting to form.
context: Used a Dutch oven this time. The crust crackled when it came out. Progress.

title: Advanced Sourdough Hydration: 80%+ Doughs
context: High-hydration techniques for open crumb — stretch and fold vs coil fold. Getting technical now.

title: Sourdough Discard Recipes: Crackers, Pancakes, Pizza
context: Using excess starter — zero waste baking. The discard is an ingredient, not waste.

title: I notice the sourdough rhythm is the opposite of my work rhythm
context: It forces patience. You can't rush fermentation. Maybe that's why I'm drawn to it right now — it's medicine for my acceleration problem.

title: Saved 47 things this week. In January it was 12/week. The acceleration is back.
context: The pattern I described in January — the acceleration before the crash. I can see it now. Can the tool see it too?

title: Am I accelerating again?
context: Pattern recognition: the same intake velocity that preceded the December crash. But this time I can see it. Is seeing it enough?

title: What could I say to you that would be of value, except that perhaps you seek too much — Hesse
context: Siddhartha. The seeking itself becomes the obstacle. At some point you have to stop collecting and start being.

title: Reflecting on three months of saves
context: The collection tells a story: someone building a tool to understand themselves, planning a wedding that reflects their values, learning patience through bread, and struggling with their own energy.

title: The four threads: building (Mycelium), celebrating (wedding), slowing down (sourdough), surviving (energy). They're all connected.
context: Each thread is a different response to the same question: how do I live intentionally in a world that rewards speed?
